messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Critical alert - api-prod 5xx spike detected (>3% over 5m). Alerts firing: api-gateway-5xx-rate, upstream-timeout-rate. See /incidents/1842109876 for details.
emma: acked. I’m on it, pulling logs and current deploys.
leo: thx emma. any service-level scope? customers complaining?
sara: monitoring shows 5xx mainly on /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings, 90% are 504 gateway timeouts, some 502s.
emma: good catch. likely upstream provider (edge-proxy) or our ingress layer. Running quick dpkg: `kubectl get pods -n api -l app=gateway -o wide`
leo: I see higher latencies on gateway pods, CPU ~85% and connection resets. Could be connection pool exhaustion.
raj: paging infra team for edge-proxy. @infra-bot can you validate upstream health?
infra-bot: edge-proxy cluster in us-west-2 shows degraded nodes: 2/6 nodes reporting high connection errors. Root cause: increased retry storms from clients.
emma: mitigation plan: 1) scale gateway replicas by +3 2) enable short-circuit fallback for heavy endpoints 3) add temporary rate-limit for noisy customers 4) failover to dedicated capacity for VIPs. Who can apply scale?
leo: I’ll patch HPA and increase replica count now. Patch command: `kubectl scale deploy/gateway --replicas=8 -n api`
sara: applying fallback config now (runtime feature flag): `PATCH /config/runtime` payload: `{"gateway.fallback":true, "fallback.mode":"fast-500-to-200"}`
emma: notifying support to update customer-facing status page: "Partial degradation for API endpoints in us-west-2: elevated timeouts and 5xx"
incident-bot: Note: alert auto-escalation disabled for this incident by emma.
leo: replicas up, arming additional connection pool tuning on nodes.
raj: infra confirmed edge-proxy is flapping due to a bad upstream NAT gateway in provider region. They're routing traffic around bad nodes. Post-failover errors trending down.
sara: 5xx rate dropped from 3.6% -> 0.9% over 7 minutes, timeouts still sporadic.
emma: excellent. keep monitoring for 30m and then decide on alert threshold updates and runbook updates. We need to avoid churning on this kind of transient provider fault.
leo: suggest follow-ups: - add alert grouping by upstream provider - increase alert window from 5m->10m for 5xx-rate - add synthetic health check hitting /health and /v1/generate with small payloads
raj: +1. also add a cooldown and mute policy for known provider failovers so we don't wake infra repeatedly.
sara: I'm creating an incident ticket and adding actions. Ticket: INC-1842109876 - gateway 5xx spike - mitigation & tuning.
emma: handing off to raj for long-running follow-ups after my shift. raj, please own alert tuning and dashboard work. I'll add notes to the incident doc.
raj: taking handoff. summary in inc doc: cause = upstream provider NAT flapping causing connection resets -> gateway pool exhaustion -> 504/502. Mitigation = scale gateway, enable fallback, temporary rate-limits, provider routing.
infra-bot: Deploy logs: route-change completed at 2026-03-07T21:05:12Z, provider acknowledged transient NAT issues.
leo: small proposal for alert rule changes (PromQL):
```
# previous: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",job="api-gateway"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[5m])) > 0.005
# proposed: use longer window + noise suppression
sum_over_time(
  (rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",job="api-gateway"}[1m]))[10m:1m]
) / sum_over_time((rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[1m]))[10m:1m]) > 0.01
```
This switches to 10m rolling and raises threshold to 1% while we add grouping.
sara: also recommend alert label by upstream_provider and service, so we can mute provider-wide issues.
emma: agreed. raj, add two tasks: change alert to 10m window & group by provider; create a new dashboard for upstream failures with synthetic checks. add regression test to CI for alert firing.
raj: noted. ETA for alert rule and dashboard: 24h. I’ll pair with leo on synthetic check.
leo: I’ll also add a dashboard panel showing connection errors per provider and a sparklines for 504 vs 502 vs 500.
sara: post-incident: we should update runbook section "Upstream provider flapping" with explicit mitigation sequence (scale, fallback, provider-route, customer-notify).
emma: yes, and assign RCA owner after stabilizing. No blame, focus on process.
incident-bot: Incident INC-1842109876 marked stable at 1842110200 by emma.
raj: quick note for postmortem: action items = alert rule change, dashboard, runbook update, provider SLA follow-up, synthetic test. I’ll schedule RCA meeting tomorrow 09:00 PST.
leo: leaving a small notes snippet to include in the PM: `kubectl describe pod gateway-xxx` showed repeated `tcp_reset` logs from envoy, matching provider nat errors.
sara: support reported ~12 customer complaints; most were retrying and got transient failures. Sent proactive messages to top 5 affected customers.
emma: handing off fully. thanks team. I’m off shift - ping raj for follow-ups. :wave:
raj: thanks emma. I’ll post updates in this thread as items complete.
infra-bot: reminder: please attach alert change PR link to incident doc before merging.
leo: will open PR: `github.com/redwood/alerts/pull/482` - contains modified rule and alert grouping.
raj: closing handoff. I’ll make sure we don't revert alert sensitivity without incident review.
incident-bot: Thread archived for long-term follow-up."
